dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Yes, I'm calling about water coming out of a pipe at the curb. It's running onto the sidewalk and it's freezing. I've called about this before and I expect I'll be told the same thing.
Okay, let's see what we can do. Can you tell me where this is?
392 Bliss Road. Easton's Beach side. Down toward the water end.
392 Bliss Road. And you said there's a pipe at the curb with water coming out of it?

That's right. A pipe in the curb, the water just trickles out of it. It's not raining, hasn't rained in days. It's dry out. But it runs across the sidewalk and by this time of day, with the cold, it's a sheet of ice. Somebody's going to go down.
So no storm, just a steady flow of water, and it's icing over on the sidewalk. Is that it?
Yes. Every morning it's worse. I manage the property, I'm not out there skating around on it myself, but the tenants have to walk it.
Understood. Have you reported this before?
I called a while back and somebody told me Bliss Road is a state road. So it wasn't the city's problem. That was the end of that. Nobody told me who to call instead.

Okay. [pause] I see. Well, some of the roads out that way are state-maintained, that's true, and the drainage along them can belong to the state too. But I don't want to just send you away again. Let me ask you a couple of things. Is the pipe coming out of the curb itself, or out of the ground right next to it?
Out of the curb. A little round opening, I'd say. Like a drain outlet. The water comes out clear, doesn't smell.
Clear and no smell. And it's running all day, not just now and then?
Seems to be all day. I've seen it at different hours. It's running now.

All right. Here's what I can do. I'll write this up and send it over to our highway people so they can look at whether that outlet is something the city owns. If it turns out to be the state's, they'd be the ones to pass it along to the state's highway office. And I'll tell you who you'd call yourself, so you aren't stuck.
That would be a change. Who would I call? The state?

The state's transportation department has a maintenance office, and they take reports on state roads. I don't have their direct line in front of me, so I'd have you look it up under the state's transportation department, and ask for maintenance for this area. But I'll make our report first, so it's on record that you called today.
Fine. Put that I called today, Monday. And that it was also reported before.

Will do. Let me read it back. Water running continuously from a curb outlet at 392 Bliss Road, Easton's Beach side, no recent storm, freezing on the sidewalk, caller was previously told it's a state road. Caller is the property manager. Is that right?

That's right. And one more thing, the people next door are moving out this weekend. It may be their pipe, or their line, I don't know. But the house will be empty after that, so nobody will be around to notice it.
Okay, that's useful. So the neighboring house is being vacated this weekend. I'll add that, in case someone needs to check whether it's coming from the property. Could I get a number to reach you?
401-555-0178. And your name?
Carol Almy. A-L-M-Y.

Thank you, Ms. Almy. I'll get this to the highway crew today. If it's one of ours, they'll want to look at it soon with the ice. In the meantime, if you have sand or salt you can put on that stretch of sidewalk, that would help until someone gets out there.
I'll have somebody put some down. I'm not out there with a shovel at my age.
Of course. And if you don't hear back from us in a couple of days, call and ask for me, Lorraine, and I'll check where it stands.
All right. We'll see. Thank you.
You're welcome. Stay warm, and have a good holiday week.
